text:
olivia: Headsup — GlacierPay reporting 429s starting ~2026-03-12T01:15Z, sustained for ~20m. Customer says spikes line up with a bunch of scheduled cron jobs. Error rate ~15% of requests during the window. Can SRE + platform look?

kevin: Looking. Do we have the exact RPM/TPM numbers they see and any request ids?

olivia: They sent a screenshot: 270 RPM averaging, peaks ~520 RPM for a few 10s. TPM ~14k over the 20m window. No request ids in the screenshot, but they gave an example curl with their API key (we redacted) that reproduces immediately.

nima: Quick checklist: are they hitting per-minute bucket limits (our legacy per-minute window) vs rolling window? If their cron fires at top-of-minute multiple times from many hosts, that concentrates traffic into minute boundaries.

kevin: On our side: seeing a matching spike in ratecap errors on the EU edge around 01:15Z. 429s include headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 300/min`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 30`. So it's the RPM cap.

olivia: Customer runs 12 Lambda-ish workers that all wake at the same minute and fan out 30 requests each. So yeah, synchronized. They asked for immediate mitigations.

nima: Short-term mitigations we can suggest to them: add jitter to their cron sleeps, randomize schedule across minutes, lower concurrent streams, and implement exponential backoff with jitter on client retries. Also increase client-side connection keepalive to reuse HTTP/1.1 or reduce HTTP/2 multiplexing pressure.

kevin: On infra side we can: 1) temporarily raise their per-minute quota for the tenant if contract allows; 2) enable a rolling-window smoothing policy on their route (if allowed) to convert minute buckets into a short sliding window; or 3) recommend Dedicated capacity. Which one do we want to offer now?

olivia: Sales/CS prefer we try a temporary quota bump first while we advise them on scheduling fixes. I'll confirm with account team.

nima: Also note: if they're using token sharing (same API key across many processes) the per-key limit will be hit faster. Ask them to check for token reuse and any SDK misconfig (e.g., re-initialize client per request).

kevin: Can you ask for a small repro script? A minimal curl loop is ideal. Example to reproduce:

```
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null &
  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```

kevin: Also capture response headers for a 429 to confirm the exact limit window semantics.

olivia: Sent repro request to customer template with the above and a request for a short recording of their cron timings.

ops-bot: Note: created ticket RI-4821 and applied staging quota +20% for GlacierPay until 2026-03-12T05:00Z. Audit log: quota_change_by=kevin.

nima: If we bump quota, add a temporary rate-limit rule to avoid blown-out spikes affecting other tenants. We can add a per-customer smoothing policy (throttle by qps with leaky bucket) — low risk.

kevin: Follow-ups: please attach one 429 response (headers + body), the repro script output, and approximate client machine count. I can then run a replay against our staging ratecap to confirm behavior and test the smoothing rule.

olivia: Will gather and update ticket. For now told customer: (1) add jitter to cron, (2) implement exponential backoff (0.5s * 2^n + jitter), (3) we can temporarily raise quota while we coordinate. They replied :thumbsup:.

nima: One more note to customer to avoid repeated immediate retries on 429 — recommend honoring `Retry-After` header and randomizing retry windows.

kevin: I'll schedule a short replay exercise in staging and post logs in the ticket.

olivia: Thanks team — updating GlacierPay and closing loop once they push changes.
